key_insight: Asymptomatic female carriers of the XDP-linked TAF1 variant already show clear striatal neurodegeneration and iron accumulation on MRI, even without overt clinical symptoms.
clinical_relevance: This suggests female carriers may have subclinical brain changes that could matter for risk stratification and future monitoring, but not for diagnosis or treatment decisions by itself.
method: 103 female relatives of XDP patients were assessed with clinical testing, genetic screening, and multimodal MRI.
MRI analyses included voxel-based morphometry, subcortical volumetry, and susceptibility-weighted imaging for iron.
A subset had longitudinal follow-up MRI to look for progression over time.
evidence_signal: Compared with healthy controls, 42 female carriers had significantly smaller caudate, putamen, and pallidum volumes, higher caudate iron signal, and strong age/estimated-onset correlations, but no clear short-term longitudinal progression.
watch_item: The follow-up window was relatively short and the findings are observational, so the MRI changes do not yet establish how or when subclinical abnormalities translate into clinical disease.
paper_title: Preclinical Basal Ganglia Neurodegeneration in Female X Linked Dystonia Parkinsonism Carriers
